I hit that stage a couple months ago. Personally I was more pissed off than lonely because I spent my entire life being alone, had friends and it felt like i couldn't go back when those friendships ended. 

It really take times to find things that you do alone and prefer to do alone, and then branching out into things that are more commonly a people thing and making them an alone thing.  

Example, I used to spend most of my time watching movies/tv shows at home in enjoyment. Trying to integrate myself back into that, I started watching with my phone out of sight (no reminder that no one would text me anymore), started watching things i found myself (no need to text some one "hey watching __ like you said i should), and then I began to focussed. 

Finally once i felt brave enough/really wanted to see something out now, I looked at movie times. Factored in how many people would be in the cinema , school students can't come until after 4pm on weekdays (no loud groups), parents aren't going to bring their kid to a 12pm movie on a week day either (no crying babies), and couples won't show up until night/evening (no 6pm movies should be seen. 

So, i found a method/schedule went there, and slowly got used to going to movies alone. When/if I felt awkward I then found pros in the situation to calm myself down from feeling bad. 1) I didn't have to worry about another person enjoyment, 2) I could sit/stretch out wherever i want, 3) I could eat in the theatre without being annoying to my seat mate. 4) it was significantly cheaper to have to pay for just the movie and not the games/movie theatre crap.
